title: DbmDB.set / SqliteDB.set initialize empty cache on miss, discarding persisted task data on dump
claim: DbmDB.set and SqliteDB.set initialize an empty dict for a task that exists in persistent storage but is absent from the in-memory cache, so a subsequent dump() silently overwrites the stored record with only the newly set key, erasing sibling dependency values.

title: PythonAction.execute mutates global sys.stdout/sys.stderr unsafely under MThreadRunner
claim: PythonAction.execute replaces process-global sys.stdout and sys.stderr to capture output, which is not thread-safe under MThreadRunner: concurrent Python actions can capture each other's output or restore the wrong streams.

title: Exceptions in CmdAction reader threads are silently discarded and never propagated to execute()
claim: Exceptions raised inside the _print_process_output reader threads (t_out, t_err) are not propagated back to CmdAction.execute() via Thread.join(), so output-processing failures are silently dropped; as a secondary consequence, a thread that stops draining its pipe can cause the child process to block on a full buffer, deadlocking the parent.

title: Top-level pyflakes import in dodo.py breaks all doit commands and tests when pyflakes is absent
claim: dodo.py imports pyflakes at module level, causing every doit invocation (and the CLI test suite subprocess) to fail with exit code 3 in environments where pyflakes is not installed, even for commands unrelated to linting.

title: SqliteDB._sqlite3 registers process-global SQLite adapters and converters
claim: SqliteDB._sqlite3 calls sqlite3.register_adapter and sqlite3.register_converter for list, dict, and the 'json' column type; these registries are process-global, so they affect every SQLite connection in the host process and can break embedding applications that use sqlite3 independently.

title: Exceptions from subprocess.Popen escape CmdAction.execute unwrapped
claim: Exceptions raised by subprocess.Popen itself (missing executable, bad working directory, permission error) are not caught in CmdAction.execute, so they escape as raw OSError/ValueError instead of being wrapped in TaskError, bypassing reporter formatting and --continue handling.

title: _prepare_kwargs binds only positional args, allowing doit metadata to silently overwrite explicit keyword arguments
claim: _prepare_kwargs calls bind_partial(*args) with positional arguments only, so explicitly supplied keyword arguments (e.g. targets=...) are absent from bound_args.arguments and get silently overwritten when doit injects its metadata keys.
